subject: English
description: Covers Subject-Verb Agreement error of proximity.

questions.stem: Identify the grammatical error in the following sentence: 'One of the boys have lost his backpack.'
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The subject of the sentence is 'One', which is singular. The phrase 'of the boys' is just a prepositional phrase modifying 'One'. Because the subject 'One' is singular, the verb must also be singular. Therefore, 'have' should be 'has'. The correct sentence is: "One of the boys HAS lost his backpack."
DECOY BUSTING: Students often look at the plural noun 'boys' immediately preceding the verb and mistakenly assume the verb should be plural ('have'). This is called an error of proximity.
EXAM INSIGHT: Rule: "One of / Each of / Either of / Neither of" + Plural Noun + SINGULAR VERB.
